questions.q: What three services does the capstone require, at minimum?
options: catalog, checkout, and catalog-db
frontend, backend, and cache
catalog, checkout, and a load balancer
One combined service that does everything
questions.explain: The brief scopes the project to exactly three services: catalog (the product-catalog app), checkout (which talks to catalog and the database), and catalog-db (Postgres).

questions.q: Why does catalog-db need a named volume instead of just writing to the container's own filesystem?
options: Named volumes make the database run faster
Without it, the database's data is lost whenever the container is removed or recreated
Docker requires every service to have a volume
It's required for the image to build at all
questions.explain: A container's writable layer is removed along with the container. A named volume keeps the database's data directory outside that layer, so it survives `docker compose down` and container recreation.

questions.q: Why does the rubric call for a user-defined bridge network instead of Docker's default bridge?
options: The default bridge network doesn't allow more than two containers
A user-defined network gives containers reliable name-based service discovery, which the default bridge doesn't provide
User-defined networks are required for health checks to work
It makes the containers run as non-root automatically
questions.explain: On a user-defined network, Docker's embedded DNS lets containers reach each other by service name (like `catalog-db`). The legacy default bridge network doesn't offer that automatic name resolution.

questions.q: Why does the rubric require a health check on catalog-db along with a restart policy and depends_on on checkout?
options: So checkout starts before catalog-db to save time
So checkout doesn't begin taking traffic before catalog-db is actually ready to accept connections, not just started
Health checks are only cosmetic and don't change startup behavior
So the images build faster
questions.explain: A container can report as "started" before the process inside it is actually ready. A health check plus a `depends_on` condition lets checkout wait until catalog-db is genuinely ready, not just running.

questions.q: Why must database credentials go into an untracked .env file instead of being written directly into compose.yaml?
options: compose.yaml doesn't support environment variables at all
compose.yaml is typically committed to the repo, so hardcoded credentials there would be committed and exposed too
.env files are required by Docker to start any container
It makes the containers start faster
questions.explain: compose.yaml is meant to be checked into version control. Secrets belong in a `.env` file that's covered by `.gitignore`, referenced by variable name in compose.yaml, so credentials never end up in the repo's history.
